clue.text: After chairperson's brief presentation, it proceeds

indicators.note: a brief form of a word is a shortened one, so the title is clipped to its usual abbreviation

parts.note: a professor holds a university chair; the title is shortened in everyday use
taken as written

explanation.surface: A meeting where the chair gives a short talk and then business moves on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' looks like a verb continuing the meeting, but it is the noun for money taken in; a chair-holder is a professor, shortened to PROF.
explanation.definitionFit: The proceeds of a sale or venture are the money it brings in, which is its gain or return.

clue.text: Tease a large gathering

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old verb for banter or mock good-humouredly
second meaning: a mass meeting of supporters

explanation.surface: Someone teasing a big crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'tease' sense is old-fashioned and mostly met in crosswords: to rally someone is to chaff them.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense means to chaff or ridicule playfully; the noun is a mass assembly of people for a cause.

clue.text: Fighter pilot has to stand by, we hear

parts.note: to pilot an aircraft is to fly it

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the second word counts by its sound and is spelt differently

parts.note: to stand by is to wait, which is said like the word for heaviness

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot told to stand by for orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter pilot' reads as one phrase about an air force, but the boxer is the definition and the pilot starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyweight is a boxer in the lightest standard weight class, so a fighter in the ring.

clue.text: Formidable person in two man crew?

wordplay.note: a tar is a sailor, a man of a ship's crew; two of them side by side

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fearsome individual is part of a two-person crew.
explanation.walkthrough: TAR is crossword shorthand for a sailor; the question mark flags the playful reading of the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartar is a fierce, intractable or demanding person who is hard to deal with.

clue.text: Pool money initially for wool

indicators.note: initially says that this piece comes at the start, ahead of the other one

parts.note: cash is money
a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: Pooling funds at the start to buy wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool money' reads as a phrase about sharing funds; it is two separate pieces, put in order by 'initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool from the Kashmir goat, used for knitwear.

clue.text: Alternative suggestion from bartender

parts.note: surface reading: a different plan put forward in reply to another
setter's reading: an offer made by someone standing behind the bar, the counter of a pub

explanation.walkthrough: The bartender works behind a counter, so any proposal they make comes literally from the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: This compound means a rival offer made in response to an initial bid or plan in negotiation.

clue.text: Instrument producing incidental note? Odd
Where you might see the Italian chap around

definitions.text: Where you might see the Italian chap around

indicators.note: around says one word wraps itself about the other

parts.note: a chap is a man
il is the Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: Where you might spot an Italian man about town.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, since an Italian man is just what you would see in that city.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is a major city of northern Italy, so Italian men are seen around its streets.

clue.text: For example, Arab people rough in speech

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

indicators.note: in speech means the word is taken by how it is said aloud, not by its spelling

parts.note: a rough voice is hoarse, said the same as the animal

explanation.surface: A rough-spoken example of Arab people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' looks like a nationality, but here it is the breed of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arab is a famous horse breed, often bred for speed, and so is an example of a horse used for racing.

clue.text: Acts collectively to establish recreation area

parts.note: a play is a set of acts taken together
to ground something is to base or establish it

explanation.surface: Performers working together to set up a leisure space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts' looks like a verb, but it is the plural noun: the acts of a drama, taken together.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground is an outdoor space set aside for children to play and amuse themselves.

clue.text: Strange clue for fish

indicators.note: strange suggests something made odd or unfamiliar, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solver puzzling over an odd clue whose answer is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Luce is an old name, now used chiefly in heraldry, for the pike, a predatory freshwater species.

clue.text: A kind manner — but parted with no change?

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
a cast, as in cast of mind, is a manner or bent

explanation.surface: A pleasant way of behaving, yet someone left without being given their change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parted' looks like parting company, but it means given parts in plays; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A typecast actor keeps being given the same sort of role, so the parts never vary.

clue.text: In drab surroundings, hard or tender?

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word that surrounds it

parts.note: dingy means drab and dull; the drab thing forms the surroundings
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Asking whether something in dreary surroundings is tough or soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like the opposite of hard, but it is a noun: a boat serving a larger vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a small boat that ferries people and supplies to a ship, and a dinghy is such a craft.

clue.text: Catch on a small branch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal British verb for grasp or understand
second meaning: a thin shoot of a tree

explanation.surface: Something getting snagged on a slender bough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch on' reads as snagging on the branch; it means to understand, informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to realise or grasp suddenly; the noun is a slender woody shoot growing from a bough.

clue.text: Accept one appears a little tedious

parts.note: British informal: to wear an idea is to accept or tolerate it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone finding a thing they must accept rather boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little tedious' reads as a mild judgement; 'a little' belongs to the wordplay and 'tedious' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome tires you out through dullness or monotony, which is what boring work does.

clue.text: More vigorous squadron leader's game

parts.note: round can mean brisk or vigorous, as in a round pace

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the word for an air force unit supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: An RAF commander playing a game with extra energy.

explanation.definitionFit: Rounders is a bat-and-ball team sport played mostly in British schools, similar to baseball.

clue.text: Medic attempts to absorb new principles

parts.note: a doc is a doctor

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: tries are attempts
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A doctor trying to take in fresh ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctrines are sets of beliefs or teachings held by a church, party or school of thought.

clue.text: Rum shortly available outside Oriental inn

parts.note: taken as written
E for East, the Orient

explanation.definitionFit: Hostelry is an old-fashioned or jocular word for a pub or hotel offering lodging and drink.

clue.text: Pony in race, partly Arab type

clue.text: Sailors exulted

explanation.definitionFit: A crew is the body of people working a ship; crew is also an old past form of crow, to boast triumphantly.

clue.text: Regular class a learner joins

taken as written
L for learner, from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars

clue.text: Lobby on behalf of the old captive

explanation.definitionFit: A foyer is an entrance hall in a theatre, hotel or block of flats, also called a lobby.

clue.text: Start working square pattern superimposed on circle

the letter shaped like a circle

clue.text: Quality of wine, not spirit

clue.text: Barely in time to continue, note

taken as written
L for libra, the pound sterling

clue.text: Not so much performing as teaching
